summary.text: Matt Longjohn is a Democratic state representative from Michigan House District 40 who took office on January 1, 2025, and is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election. He is a physician and public health professional.

paragraphs.text: Matt Longjohn was born in Kalamazoo, Michigan, and earned a bachelor's degree from Kalamazoo College in 1993, an M.D. from Tulane University in 1999, and a graduate degree from the Tulane University School of Public Health and Tropical Medicine in 2003.

He has been affiliated with the WMU Homer J Stryker School of Medicine, Epiphany Health Consulting, the Partnership to Align Social Care, the City of Portage Planning Commission and Kalamazoo Area Runners.

In a 2024 Ballotpedia survey, Longjohn described himself as a fifth-generation Kalamazoo County resident who had served in nonprofit executive roles for most of the previous 25 years, said he ran for U.S. Congress in 2018, and said Governor Whitmer appointed him to the Protect Michigan Commission in 2020.
He listed health equity, health care access and affordability, prescription drug prices, reproductive freedoms, mental and behavioral health, and the health care workforce among his priorities.

Longjohn assumed office in the Michigan House on January 1, 2025, advanced from the Democratic primary on August 4, 2026, and in the 2025-2026 session sits on the House Appropriations Committee and the Select Committee on Protecting Michigan Employees and Small Businesses.
